Problem: Arnel had ten boxes of pencils with the same number of pencils in each box.  He kept ten pencils and shared the remaining pencils equally with his five friends. If his friends got eight pencils each, how many pencils are in each box?
Program:
target:
collection("arnel.pencil_boxes", "box", "arnel", source("ten boxes of pencils"))
collection("arnel.pencils", "pencil", "arnel", source("ten boxes of pencils"))
collection("arnel.friends", "friend", "arnel", source("his five friends"))
collection("arnel.friends.pencils", "pencil", "arnel.friends", source("shared the remaining pencils equally with his five friends"))
observe(at("arnel.pencil_boxes.count", "initial"), 10, "count", source("ten boxes of pencils"))
product_relation(at("arnel.pencils.count", "initial"), at("arnel.pencil_boxes.count", "initial"), "arnel.pencil_boxes.pencils_per_box", source("ten boxes of pencils with the same number of pencils in each box"))
transfer("share_pencils", "arnel", at("arnel.pencils.count", "current"), "arnel.friends.pencils", "arnel.pencils.shared.count", source("shared the remaining pencils equally with his five friends"))
observe(at("arnel.pencils.count", "current"), 10, "count", source("He kept ten pencils"))
observe(at("arnel.friends.count", "current"), 5, "count", source("his five friends"))
observe(at("arnel.friends.each.pencils.count", "current"), 8, "count", source("his friends got eight pencils each"))
product_relation("arnel.pencils.shared.count", at("arnel.friends.count", "current"), at("arnel.friends.each.pencils.count", "current"), source("shared the remaining pencils equally with his five friends"))
query("value", "arnel.pencil_boxes.pencils_per_box")

Problem: Jessica was trying to win a gift card to her favorite store.  To win, she had to guess the total number of red & white jelly beans in the bowl of mixed color jelly beans. She figured it would take three bags of jelly beans to fill up the fishbowl.  She assumed that each bag of jellybeans had a similar distribution of colors in each bag.  She bought one bag of jellybeans and separated them by color.  She had 24 red, 13 black, 36 green, 28 purple, 32 yellow and 18 white.  What was Jessica's guess as to how many red and white jelly beans were in the fishbowl?
Program:
target:
collection("jessica.sample_bags", "bag", "jessica", source("one bag of jellybeans"))
add("buy_sample_bag", "jessica", at("jessica.sample_bags.count", "current"), 1, source("bought one bag of jellybeans"))
collection("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans", "jellybean", "jessica.sample_bag", source("one bag of jellybeans"))
collection("fishbowl.jellybeans", "jellybean", "fishbowl", source("three bags of jelly beans to fill up the fishbowl"))
observe(at("fishbowl.jellybean_bag_capacity.count", "current"), 3, "count", source("three bags of jelly beans to fill up the fishbowl"))
observe(at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.red.count", "current"), 24, "count", source("24 red"))
observe(at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.black.count", "current"), 13, "count", source("13 black"))
observe(at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.green.count", "current"), 36, "count", source("36 green"))
observe(at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.purple.count", "current"), 28, "count", source("28 purple"))
observe(at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.yellow.count", "current"), 32, "count", source("32 yellow"))
observe(at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.white.count", "current"), 18, "count", source("18 white"))
multiple(at("fishbowl.jellybeans.red.count", "estimated"), at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.red.count", "current"), 3, source("She figured it would take three bags of jelly beans to fill up the fishbowl.  She assumed that each bag of jellybeans had a similar distribution of colors in each bag"))
multiple(at("fishbowl.jellybeans.black.count", "estimated"), at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.black.count", "current"), 3, source("She figured it would take three bags of jelly beans to fill up the fishbowl.  She assumed that each bag of jellybeans had a similar distribution of colors in each bag"))
multiple(at("fishbowl.jellybeans.green.count", "estimated"), at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.green.count", "current"), 3, source("She figured it would take three bags of jelly beans to fill up the fishbowl.  She assumed that each bag of jellybeans had a similar distribution of colors in each bag"))
multiple(at("fishbowl.jellybeans.purple.count", "estimated"), at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.purple.count", "current"), 3, source("She figured it would take three bags of jelly beans to fill up the fishbowl.  She assumed that each bag of jellybeans had a similar distribution of colors in each bag"))
multiple(at("fishbowl.jellybeans.yellow.count", "estimated"), at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.yellow.count", "current"), 3, source("She figured it would take three bags of jelly beans to fill up the fishbowl.  She assumed that each bag of jellybeans had a similar distribution of colors in each bag"))
multiple(at("fishbowl.jellybeans.white.count", "estimated"), at("jessica.sample_bag.jellybeans.white.count", "current"), 3, source("She figured it would take three bags of jelly beans to fill up the fishbowl.  She assumed that each bag of jellybeans had a similar distribution of colors in each bag"))
collection("fishbowl.jellybeans.red_and_white", "jellybean", "fishbowl", source("red and white jelly beans were in the fishbowl"))
member("fishbowl.jellybeans.red_and_white", "fishbowl.jellybeans.red", source("red and white jelly beans"))
member("fishbowl.jellybeans.red_and_white", "fishbowl.jellybeans.white", source("red and white jelly beans"))
query("sum", "fishbowl.jellybeans.red_and_white", "estimated")

Problem: Jack is making barbecue sauce. He uses 3 cups of ketchup, 1 cup of vinegar and 1 cup of honey. If each burger takes 1/4 cup of sauce and each pulled pork sandwich takes 1/6 cup, how many burgers can Jack make if he makes 18 pulled pork sandwiches?
Program:
target:
observe(at("jack.barbecue_sauce.ketchup.volume", "initial"), 3, "cup", source("3 cups of ketchup"))
observe(at("jack.barbecue_sauce.vinegar.volume", "initial"), 1, "cup", source("1 cup of vinegar"))
observe(at("jack.barbecue_sauce.honey.volume", "initial"), 1, "cup", source("1 cup of honey"))
sum_relation(at("jack.barbecue_sauce.volume", "initial"), at("jack.barbecue_sauce.ketchup.volume", "initial"), at("jack.barbecue_sauce.vinegar.volume", "initial"), at("jack.barbecue_sauce.honey.volume", "initial"), source("He uses 3 cups of ketchup, 1 cup of vinegar and 1 cup of honey"))
observe(at("jack.pulled_pork_sandwiches.count", "scenario"), 18, "count", source("18 pulled pork sandwiches"))
consume("make_pulled_pork_sandwiches", "jack", at("jack.barbecue_sauce.volume", "current"), fraction(at("jack.pulled_pork_sandwiches.count", "scenario"), 1, 6), source("each pulled pork sandwich takes 1/6 cup, how many burgers can Jack make if he makes 18 pulled pork sandwiches"))
rate_relation(at("jack.barbecue_sauce.volume", "current"), fraction(1, 1, 4), at("jack.burgers.count", "possible"), source("each burger takes 1/4 cup of sauce"))
query("value", at("jack.burgers.count", "possible"))

Problem: Maggie went to Lou's aquarium and saw 100 goldfish in the aquarium. She asked if she could take some home to care for, and she was allowed to catch half of them. While using a catching net, she caught 3/5 of the total number of goldfish she was allowed to take home. How many goldfish does Maggie remain with to catch to get the total number she was allowed to take home?
Program:
target:
collection("lous_aquarium.goldfish", "goldfish", "lous_aquarium", source("100 goldfish in the aquarium"))
collection("maggie.goldfish.allowed", "goldfish", "maggie", source("goldfish she was allowed to take home"))
collection("maggie.goldfish.caught", "goldfish", "maggie", source("she caught 3/5 of the total number of goldfish she was allowed to take home"))
observe(at("lous_aquarium.goldfish.count", "initial"), 100, "count", source("100 goldfish in the aquarium"))
fraction_of("maggie.goldfish.allowed.count", at("lous_aquarium.goldfish.count", "initial"), 1, 2, source("she was allowed to catch half of them"))
transfer("catch_goldfish", "maggie", at("lous_aquarium.goldfish.count", "current"), at("maggie.goldfish.caught.count", "current"), fraction("maggie.goldfish.allowed.count", 3, 5), source("she caught 3/5 of the total number of goldfish she was allowed to take home"))
query("difference", event_field("catch_goldfish", "quantity"), "maggie.goldfish.allowed.count")

observe(at("nora.orange_pick_batches.third_tree.count", "current"), 120, "count", source("120 from the third tree"))

query("absolute_difference", at("matt.route.house_to_first_sign.distance", "current"), at("matt.route.house_to_second_sign.distance", "current"))

Problem: An artist uses 3 ounces of paint for every large canvas they cover, and 2 ounces of paint for every small canvas they cover.  They have completed 3 large paintings and 4 small paintings.  How many ounces of paint have they used?
Program:
target:
observe(at("artist.paint.large_canvas.rate", "current"), 3, "ounce_per_canvas", source("3 ounces of paint for every large canvas they cover"))
observe(at("artist.paint.small_canvas.rate", "current"), 2, "ounce_per_canvas", source("2 ounces of paint for every small canvas they cover"))
observe(at("artist.completed_paintings.large.count", "current"), 3, "count", source("3 large paintings"))
observe(at("artist.completed_paintings.small.count", "current"), 4, "count", source("4 small paintings"))
product_relation(at("artist.paint.used.large", "current"), at("artist.paint.large_canvas.rate", "current"), at("artist.completed_paintings.large.count", "current"), source("3 ounces of paint for every large canvas they cover"))
product_relation(at("artist.paint.used.small", "current"), at("artist.paint.small_canvas.rate", "current"), at("artist.completed_paintings.small.count", "current"), source("2 ounces of paint for every small canvas they cover"))
sum_relation(at("artist.paint.used.total", "current"), at("artist.paint.used.large", "current"), at("artist.paint.used.small", "current"), source("An artist uses 3 ounces of paint for every large canvas they cover, and 2 ounces of paint for every small canvas they cover"))
query("value", at("artist.paint.used.total", "current"))

Problem: An opera house has 150 rows; each row has ten seats. The ticket costs $10 per show. How much did the opera house earn from one of the shows if 20% of the seats were not taken?
Program:
target:
collection("opera_house.seats", "seat", "opera_house", source("An opera house has 150 rows; each row has ten seats"))
observe(at("opera_house.rows.count", "current"), 150, "count", source("An opera house has 150 rows"))
observe(at("opera_house.seats.per_row", "current"), 10, "count", source("each row has ten seats"))
product_relation(at("opera_house.seats.capacity", "current"), at("opera_house.rows.count", "current"), at("opera_house.seats.per_row", "current"), source("150 rows; each row has ten seats"))
observe(at("opera_house.ticket.price", "one_show"), 10, "dollar", source("The ticket costs $10 per show"))
percent_of(at("opera_house.seats.untaken.count", "one_show"), at("opera_house.seats.capacity", "current"), 20, source("20% of the seats were not taken"))
sum_relation(at("opera_house.seats.capacity", "current"), at("opera_house.seats.taken.count", "one_show"), at("opera_house.seats.untaken.count", "one_show"), source("20% of the seats were not taken"))
product_relation(at("opera_house.earnings", "one_show"), at("opera_house.seats.taken.count", "one_show"), at("opera_house.ticket.price", "one_show"), source("The ticket costs $10 per show. How much did the opera house earn from one of the shows if 20% of the seats were not taken?"))
query("value", at("opera_house.earnings", "one_show"))
